maria: FYI noticed a measurable drop in prefix cache hit-rate after last night's kernel rollout (attn-optimizations + kernel-selector change). p50 latency unchanged but token cost and p95 tails spiked.
chen: ugh. numbers?
maria: quick snapshot from perf dashboard: prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.45 (post-deploy). cold_start hit-rate stable ~0.9. served-requests where prefix_len>32 saw biggest drop.
jules: any model/quant changes in that deploy?
maria: deploy included: kernel-selector v3.2 (changed kernel alignment for block-attn), attention-optimizer patch, and new quant profile q4_0->q4_v2 for some model variants.
travis: could be key normalization. kernel-selector changed sequence chunking; KV keys may differ if we compute key based on (model, kv_hash, kernel_variant).
maria: exactly. I pulled some logs:
```
cache_lookup model=rw-v1 variant=q4_v2 prefix_hash=0x8af3 len=48 hit=false
cache_insert model=rw-v1 variant=q4_0 prefix_hash=0x8af3 len=48
```
jules: interesting — same prefix_hash but variant mismatch. before we treated kernel_variant as transparent; now it’s part of cache key.
chen: was that deliberate? the kernel-selector added variant to key to avoid incompatible kv encoding across kernels.
maria: yes but it causes fragmentation: same logical prefix stored under multiple keys if selector chooses different kernel for similar requests. lower aggregate hit-rate.
travis: do we have counts for kernel-switch churn?
maria: from traces: 18% of requests for rw-v1 are using variant A on GPU type gtx-x and variant B on gtx-y for identical sequences -> churn.
perf-bot: ALERT perf-regression: p95 token latency +32% in rw-v1 surfaced in infra nightly checks.
jules: hypothesis list: 1) kernel-variant-in-key increased cardinality -> lower reuse 2) quant profile differences change kv layout (needs serialization mismatch) 3) new attention tiling causes different prefix chunk boundaries -> different hash input (if we include chunk idx).
chen: quick repro: run serving binary with --force-kernel=A and then --force-kernel=B on same workload, compare cache hits. can do in staging.
maria: did quick run on staging: with forced-A hit_rate=0.71, forced-B=0.69, mixed=0.46. that matches our fragmentation theory.
travis: for short-term rollback we can revert kernel-selector change (v3.1). but it fixes some p50 micro-ops for long sequences. tradeoff.
jules: alternative: remove kernel_variant from cache key and add compatibility checks on load: i.e., detect kv encoding version and transcode if necessary (cheaper for small prefixes).
chen: transcoding code path risk? may add CPU overhead. but better than losing cache reuse.
maria: also saw interaction with batching heuristics: new batch splitter groups by alignment which reduced cross-request prefix sharing in a batch, lowering in-batch cache warmup.
travis: can we change batching to prioritize prefix hash grouping when possible? maybe a quick heuristic: prefer grouping requests with identical prefix_hash in same batch up to N.
jules: sounds good. we should also add a warmup job: when model/gpu kernel mapping flips, proactively re-populate cache for top-K prefixes using historical traffic. cheap background jobs.
maria: timeline suggestion: 1) immediate: toggle kernel-selector flag to v3.1 on canary (rollback if stable) 2) short-term (2d): remove variant from cache key and add runtime compatibility guard 3) medium (1w): implement grouping-by-prefix in batcher + warmup job 4) long: refactor KV serialization to be kernel-agnostic.
chen: I'll open a rollback PR and a follow-up issue for keying change. assign to runtime-team.
travis: logging: add metric prefix_cache.shards and variant_cardinality per model so we can monitor fragmentation.
maria: added screenshots and sample trace ids in the incident doc. linking: https://redwood/internal/perf/1749812345
jules: +1. also add a guarded experiment for transcoding CPU cost: sample 1% of traffic with variant-agnostic loads and measure cpu and latency.
perf-bot: NOTE: added perf-alert tag and created ticket INF-1248.
chen: thanks — I'll coordinate deploy rollback and post back with results. :thumbsup:
